findings.text: Red condition is correct. desktopCheckFailed sets desktopStatus and desktopCheckFailure to the same string, so equality is true only for a failed check. Any later progress text overwrites desktopStatus, so it differs from the still-set desktopCheckFailure and renders secondary. desktopCheckFailure == nil never matches the non-optional String. Only the foreground style changed; the Text and the !desktopReady guard are unchanged. Residual: the red is a string-equality heuristic, so if progress text ever equalled the failure text it would be red; not realistic.

Timeout mapping fires only in the intended case. DesktopAppWorkflow.transient() treats every ClaudeObservationError (including otherPage) as retryable, so wait() rethrows otherPage only when it is the last error at the 8 s deadline (lastError is cleared by any successful read). The catch is scoped to ClaudeObservationError.otherPage, inside the foreground-only branch, after the claude://claude.ai/new launch and before any composer interaction or send, so 'Nothing was sent.' is accurate: this path never types or clicks send. Other errors (transient, incompleteSnapshot, dialogs, changed-while-verifying) pass through unchanged. If the last read was a readable non-new chat that never became new, wait() already throws the same failure string. The same string is used for both, so wording is consistent.

Behavior change: a persistently-other page now surfaces as DesktopAppError.unavailable rather than ClaudeObservationError.otherPage, so WebAgentSession's `catch ClaudeObservationError.otherPage where sending` (line ~1667) cannot match an error from this branch. That handler would only see otherPage from a non-foreground/other path. I did not trace that handler's intent beyond confirming the new-chat attempt had already been made, so a hint-style message there would have been misleading anyway. No test in the repo references either string; no test was added for the new mapping (SHOULD-NOT-BLOCK, suggest a unit test with a fake clock where read always throws otherPage).
